_meta.feast: St John the Theologian, Apostle and Evangelist (with St Arsenius the Great)
_meta._note: May 8 commemorates both St John the Theologian (apostle/evangelist — principal) and St Arsenius the Great (venerable one). May 8 falls in the Pentecostarion period (between Pascha and Pentecost), so the rubric specifies a Pentecostarion canon + theotokia + sessional hymns intertwined with the saint material. This file captures only St John (Canon of the holy evangelist by John of Damascus, Tone VIII); the Arsenius canon and the Pentecostarion overlay are omitted per the menaion-matins-track pattern (cf. similar omissions for Theotokos canons in jan-30, dec-06, etc.). Magnificat is retained at Ode 9 (no rubric suppression — Theotokion present).

troparion.text:
O beloved apostle of Christ God,
hasten thou to deliver a defenseless people.
He Who permitted thee to recline against His breast receiveth thee, prostrate in supplication.
Him do thou beseech, O theologian,
that He dispel the gloom of the nations which doth beset us,//
asking peace and great mercy for us.
troparion.label: Troparion of St John the Theologian

kontakion.text:
Who can recount thy mighty works, O virgin apostle?
For thou pourest out miracles, bringing forth a flow of healings;
and thou prayest on behalf of our souls,//
in that thou art a theologian and the beloved of Christ.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of St John the Theologian

sedalion.text:
As the disciple of Christ, the Master of all,
thou didst teach the people and illumine the world,
guiding them to the knowledge of Him, O apostle.
Wherefore, we all call thee the preacher of the Truth and Theologian,//
the friend of Christ, who reclined against His breast.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 1)
sedalion._note: Sung twice. Glory/Both-now: Sessional Hymn from the Pentecostarion (not captured here).

sedalion.text:
With hymns and sacred praises let us all hymn the most honored John,
the apostle and disciple of Christ,
who preached that the Father divinely begat Christ, our Redeemer and King;//
for he prayeth unceasingly, that our souls find mercy.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 2)
sedalion._note: Sung twice. Glory/Both-now: Sessional Hymn from the Pentecostarion.

magnification.refrain:
We magnify thee, O apostle of Christ and evangelist John the theologian,
and we honor the pangs and labors
wherewith thou didst struggle in the proclamation of the Gospel of Christ.
verses: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaimeth the work of His hands.

sessionalHymns.text:
Reclining against the breast of Jesus, thou didst receive boldness,
asking as a disciple: 'Who is Thy betrayer, Lord?'
And since thou wast exceedingly beloved, O most praised one,
He manifestly indicated the traitor to thee with a sop of bread.
Wherefore, as an initiate of ineffable mysteries,
thou teachest the incarnation of the Word to the ends of the earth.
O apostle and theologian, entreat Christ God//
that He grant forgiveness of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.
sessionalHymns.label: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleos
sessionalHymns._note: Sung twice. Glory/Both-now: Sessional Hymn from the Pentecostarion, OR the Theotokion 'Let us hymn the heavenly gate and ark…'

bothNow.text:
Let us hymn the heavenly gate and ark, the all-holy mountain, the cloud of light,
the heavenly ladder, the spiritual Paradise, the redemption of Eve,
the great treasure of the world;
because salvation for the world and forgiveness of ancient offences were wrought in her.
Therefore we cry unto her: Intercede with thine own Son and God to grant forgiveness of offences//
to those who devoutly worship thy most holy Offspring.
bothNow.label: Theotokion

prokeimenon.refrain:
Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth,
and their words unto the ends of the world.
prokeimenon.verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaimeth the work of His hands.

gospel._note: Matins Gospel of the holy evangelist.

postGospelSticheron.text:
O virgin theologian, beloved disciple of the Savior,
by thy supplications save us from all harm, we pray,//
for we are thy flock.
postGospelSticheron.label: Idiomelon of the holy evangelist

canon._author: Canon of the holy evangelist (Tone VIII). The Pentecostarion canon (4 troparia) and the Arsenius canon (4 troparia) interleaved at the actual service are omitted from this MVP file.

ode1.irmos:
The wonderworking staff of Moses, striking and dividing the sea in the figure of a cross,
once drowned Pharaoh the pursuing charioteer,
while it saved the fleeing people of Israel as they fled on foot,//
chanting a hymn unto God.

troparia.text: In so far as thou wast pure and beloved of the incorruptible light, thou didst recline, resting against His breast, and with boldness of soul didst draw forth from the Abyss of wisdom the light of understanding, O blessed Apostle John.

Theologizing supra-naturally, thou didst thunder forth, O beloved of Christ: 'In the beginning was the Word, as alive and hypostatic as His Father; and the Word was God; and the Word became flesh, and remained God immutable.'

Theotokion: If we flee from beneath thy protection, O most pure one, we are buried beneath all the perils which befall us. Wherefore, we now beseech thee: From the depths of our transgressions raise up us who have fallen, by thy divine entreaties, O pure one.

ode3.irmos:
O Christ, fortify me on the rock of Thy commandments,
Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding
and didst establish the earth upon the waters,//
for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind.

troparia.text: Among fishermen thou didst become a fisher of men and a theologian, O wise John, setting aside the love of thy father and that of the world, and with divine desire thou didst follow the Word and Master.

Having purified the eyes of thy soul, O theologian, thou didst behold the ineffable glory which doth emanate from the Word, the only-begotten Son of the Father, through Whom all things are wisely accomplished by the divine Spirit.

Theotokion: We flee beneath thy saving refuge, O Virgin Theotokos, and find salvation from the assaults of the enemy by thy supplications; whereby we are delivered from the torment which is to come, O pure one.

ode4.irmos:
Thou, O Lord, art my strength and Thou art my power,
Thou art my God and Thou art my joy,
Who without leaving the Father's bosom hast visited our lowliness;//
wherefore, with the prophet Habbakuk I cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

troparia.text: Beholding the most pure Light Who shone forth amid the darkness of the world, thou wast transformed by love; and as a beacon of piety, O John, thou didst illumine with the light of theology generations of the multitudes of nations.

Having learned that the shadowy law was given by Moses, but that divine grace came about through Christ our God, O beloved son of thunder, thou didst proclaim His divinity with the precise language of theology.

Theotokion: Thou art my protection and might, my confirmation and indestructible rampart, O most pure one, and I call upon thee: night and day preserve me from all the harm wrought by Belial, that I may glorify thee with faith and love.

ode5.irmos:
O Light never-waning, why hast Thou turned Thy face from me
and why hath the alien darkness surrounded me, wretched though I be?
But do Thou guide my steps, I implore Thee,//
and turn me back towards the light of Thy commandments.

troparia.text: Beholding the most pure Light Who shone forth amid the darkness of the world, thou wast transformed by love; and as a beacon of piety, O John, thou didst illumine with the light of theology generations of the multitudes of nations.

Having learned that the shadowy law was given by Moses, but that divine grace came about through Christ our God, O beloved son of thunder, thou didst proclaim His divinity with the precise language of theology.

Theotokion: Thou art my protection and might, my confirmation and indestructible rampart, O most pure one, and I call upon thee: night and day preserve me from all the harm wrought by Belial, that I may glorify thee with faith and love.

ode6.irmos:
The abyss of my sins and the storm of my transgressions
disquieten me and thrust me down into the depths of despondency;
but do Thou stretch forth Thy mighty arm, unto me as Thou didst to Peter,//
and save me, O my Guide.

troparia.text: Isaiah beheld in an image the Ember of the divine fire which purified his lips, and he was deemed worthy of prophecy; and thou, O blessed John, wast revealed as he who reclined upon the breast of the incarnate Word of God.

The only-begotten Word Who sitteth in the bosom of the Father was seen incarnate, O blessed John, and told thee, as the beloved initiate of His mysteries, that thou wouldst behold the incorporeal God Whom no-one can look upon.
Theotokion: Illumine my soul, O all-hymned Virgin Theotokos, having given birth to the Effulgence of the Father's glory; for, having thy true grace, we abstain from all blasphemous rhetoric.

kontakion.text:
Who can recount thy mighty works, O virgin apostle?
For thou pourest out miracles, bringing forth a flow of healings;
and thou prayest on behalf of our souls,//
in that thou art a theologian and the beloved of Christ.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the holy evangelist

troparia.text: Thou didst diligently depart from the bonds of matter, O all-blessed one, as an intercessor before God, and as a herald of divinely inspired theology thou hast taught all to cry: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

Thou didst consider gold and riches to be like grass, O all-blessed one, and by the action of God thou didst transform hay into gold when thou didst theologize concerning the Creator and Lord, crying: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

The Holy Spirit Who proceedeth from the beginningless Father have we accepted as indivisible from Thee, O only-begotten Word of God; whereby Thou didst call upon the apostles to cry aloud: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

Theotokion: Thou wast the temple and palace of Christ the King; thou alone wast the couch of Solomon, which, as saith the Scriptures, sixty of the mighty surrounded. And with thee, O Virgin, they cry aloud chanting: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

ode8.irmos:
In his wrath the Chaldean Tyrant made the furnace blaze, with heat fanned sevenfold for the servants of God;
but when he perceived that they had been saved by a greater power,
he cried aloud to the Creator and Redeemer:
'Ye children bless, ye priests praise,//
ye people, supremely exalt Him throughout all ages.'

troparia.text: As thy most glorious memory is magnificent and rightly renowned, O herald of the divinity of Christ, it shineth forth upon the Church, perfuming her with godliness. Wherefore, rejoicing, O ye faithful, we cry aloud: O ye youths bless, O ye priests praise, O ye people, supremely exalt Him throughout all ages!

Having the theologian as the leader of our choir, O Christ, we declare Thee, Who wast theologized by him, with the Father and the Spirit, to be God, and hymning the unity in governance thereof, we cry aloud: O ye youths bless, O ye priests praise, O ye people, supremely exalt Him throughout all ages!

Theotokion: O all-immaculate one, thou hast given birth to God the Word in the flesh. Him do thou beseech, that He deliver me from the fire; for, lo! my whole life hath become a burden and I have become wholly enslaved to cruel sins. Wherefore, I flee to thee, O Virgin, and call upon thee, the joyous one.

ode9.irmos:
Heaven was stricken with awe, and the ends of the earth were filled with amazement,
for God hath appeared in the flesh, and thy womb was rendered more spacious than the heavens.//
Wherefore, the ranks of men and of angels magnify thee as the Theotokos.

troparia.text: Standing before the Cross of the Master and the pure Virgin Theotokos, the beloved disciple, the pure instrument of theology, in that he himself was virginal, accepted the commission to care for her, and, becoming the guardian of the immaculate Theotokos, he is now blessed as is meet.

The Most pure One, loving thine honored and blameless life as is meet, accepted thee, who lived angelically on earth, together with thy brother, O blessed John, and declared thee the son of His own Mother, the Theotokos. With her we all call thee blessed.

Theotokion: Be thou a pillar of salvation for me, O pure one; render the hordes of the demons impotent, cutting off the tumult of temptations and misfortunes, granting me pure freedom, and bestowing upon me divine gifts in abundance.

exapostilarion.text:
As a son of thunder thou didst proclaim theology to all mankind, saying: 'In the beginning was the Word!',
O Apostle John;
for, reclining against the breast of thy Master with faith and drawing forth therefrom streams of theology,//
thou hast watered all creation.
exapostilarion.label: Exapostilarion of the holy evangelist

stichera.text:
O most wise and blessed John,
in the magnitude of thine ardor for the love of Christ thou wast the greatest of all,
a beloved disciple of the Word Who seeth all things and judgeth the whole world with the scales of justice;
and thou wast illumined, in body and mind, with the purity and the beauties of virginity,//
O divinely blessed one.

With spiritual hymns let us now praise the most honorable John as a servant of Christ,
the flower of virginity, the pleasant dwelling-place of precious virtues,
the instrument of wisdom, the temple of the Spirit,
the radiant mouth of grace,//
the most resplendent eye of the Church.

Reclining against the breast of Christ,
thou didst draw forth the waters of theology and wisdom,
and having watered the world therewith, O most excellent John,
thou hast caused the sea of ungodliness to dry up by the proper-understanding of the Trinity;
and becoming an animate pillar of cloud,//
thou dost guide us unto the heavenly inheritance.

doxastikon.text:
O evangelist John, peer of the angels, virgin theologian instructed by God,
in an Orthodox manner thou didst preach to the world,
concerning the most pure side which poured forth blood and water,//
from whence we obtain life everlasting for our souls.
